intro_cards.title: About these notes
body: 7 units · geology to population · drawn for a phone
This book is not “world geography” — it is **Eritrea**. Outcomes: read the land’s story (rocks), water, climate, plants and animals, soils, how people make a living, and who lives where.

body: Based on Geography for Grade 12, Ministry of Education, Eritrea (2011). Sketch maps are teaching diagrams, not survey maps.

units.title: Soils in Eritrea
units.intro: Soil in Eritrea is thin on steep slopes, richer in some western plains, often at risk.

cards.title: 5.1.1 Soils of the Highlands and Escarpments
body: The Highlands of Eritrea extend from south to north and are predominantly made of crystalline rocks (precambrian).
The soils of this sub-region are, therefore, derived from these rocks.
Because of this, soils derived from basaltic rocks are fine textured.
The **Hazomo depression** is a circular basin where many of the tributaries of River Mereb converge.

cards.title: 5.1.2 Soils of the Lowlands
body: Lowlands are characterized by a very low amount of rainfall and meagre vegetation.
The soils are, therefore, shallow and coarse in texture.
The amount of phosphorous is medium to high, while nitrogen and potassium contents vary from low to medium.
Soils in the Lowlands are broadly divided as soils of western plain and soils of coastal plains.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which highly fertile, clayey soil type is found south of Asmara, characterized by shrinking and cracking during dry periods?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Match basaltic profiles to geography**
Soils south of Asmara are derived from Tertiary volcanic basalts and are characterized by deep clay textures that shrink and crack when dry. These are **Basaltic soils**.

**Step 2: Conclude**
The correct answer is Basaltic soils.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Deep, fertile alluvial soils developed from recent river deposits in the circular basin of the Hazomo Plain are categorized as:
cards.why:
**Step 1: Reference Hazomo Plain soil profiles**
The deep alluvial, silty-sandy loam soils deposited in the Hazomo basin by the Mereb River are defined as **Fluvial soils**.

**Step 2: Conclude**
The correct option is Fluvial soils.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: _________ soils become crack during dry period, while sticky during wet season.
cards.why: **Basaltic soils** (often called Vertisols or Black Cotton Soils) have a high clay content. They expand and become very sticky when wet, and shrink to form deep cracks when dry.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The dominant types of soils in the coastal plains are:
cards.why: The coastal plains of Eritrea are characterized by arid conditions and high salinity. **Xerosols** (desert soils) and **Solonchaks** (salty soils) are the dominant types found there.

cards.title: 5.2 Soil Degradation in Eritrea
body: **Soil degradation** is a process through which soil loses its fertility due to the removal of top soil by water and wind.
On the average, Eritrea loses 15-20 tons of soil per hectare in a year, but in some places the loss is as high as 100 tons per hectare per year.
The rate of erosion is much higher along steep slopes than on plain areas.
More topsoil tends to be carried away where there is little vegetation as there are neither plant roots nor organic matter to bind it together.
In such places, small channels or rills may develop into large gullies, making the land less suitable for cultivation.

cards.title: Degradation
body: Erosion after trees are cut, overgrazing, steep farming without terraces, erratic rain, loss of organic matter.

cards.title: Causes of soil degradation
body: Soil degradation is the loss of fertile topsoil to water and wind. Eritrea loses about **15–20 tonnes of soil per hectare per year**, and up to 100 t/ha in some places.

**Steep slopes:** long cultivation of mountain slopes speeds up erosion. **Deforestation:** without roots and litter, runoff carries topsoil away, rills grow into gullies and leaching increases. Less than 1% of the land remains forested.

**Overgrazing:** about 80% of the land is used for grazing; overstocking strips the grass, starting near water points, so the soil is exposed and rain runs off instead of soaking in. **Results:** lower fertility and moisture, silted dams and lower food production.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: One of the following is the **result** of soil degradation?

options.B: rainfall does not sink into the ground

cards.why: Options A, C, D, and E are **causes** of soil degradation. When soil is degraded (e.g., compacted or loses organic matter), its structure breaks down, leading to reduced infiltration. As a result, rainfall cannot sink into the ground effectively, causing increased surface runoff and erosion.

cards.title: Exam question, solved
cards.problem: The most favorable condition for infiltration of rain water into the ground is a surface covered by  A) sand  B) silt and clay  C) loose rock fragments  D) compacted soil  E) A and C

steps.text: **Step 1.** Infiltration is the process by which water enters the soil. **Sand** (A) and **loose rock fragments** (C) have high porosity and permeability, allowing water to pass through easily.
**Step 2.** Silt, clay, and compacted soil have smaller pores or are blocked, which restricts water flow.

cards.title: 5.3 Measures of Soil Conservation
body: **Soil conservation** is a measure practiced for controlling soil erosion and maintaining soil fertility.
In Eritrea, farmers practice various methods of soil conservation to avoid removal of the soil.
The scientific methods of soil conservation are as follows.
The disadvantage of this method is that it takes some amount of land out of production.
Contour ploughing checks erosion and helps to retain soil and water along the furrows (c) Shelter belts Wind blows away fertile soils such as silt and clay.

cards.title: Conservation
body: Terraces and bunds, afforestation, check dams, crop rotation / manure, controlled grazing, keep vegetation on slopes.

cards.title: Link the units
body: No forest (U4) + steep geology (U1) + hard rain then drought (U3) = soil leaves for the nearest wadi (U2). Terraces fix water and soil together.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What is the dominant soil type found in the hyper-arid coastal plains south of Massawa, characterized by white, glistening surface salt crusts?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify saline soils**
Highly saline soils that accumulate surface salt crusts due to intense capillary evaporation are called **Solonchaks**.

**Step 2: Conclude**
The correct answer is Solonchaks.

glossary.meaning: Practices that control soil erosion and maintain soil fertility, e.g. terracing, tree planting and enclosures.
Loss of soil fertility and quality, mainly by removal of topsoil by water and wind.
Soil is a loose material that covers the land surface of the earth.
Soil degradation is a process through which soil loses its fertility due to the removal of top soil by water and wind.
Soil conservation is a measure practiced for controlling soil erosion and maintaining soil fertility.

tips.text: Soil is unconsolidated loose material that contains both organic and inorganic materials.
The organic materials consist of decayed plants and animals, while the inorganic components contain rocks and minerals.
In Eritrea, there are various types of soils whose classification is based on geological structure.
The soils in the Highlands and the Escarpment are predominantly derived from crystalline rocks.
In the Lowlands, the soils are shallow and course in texture because of poor process of weathering.
In the coastal plains, sandy soils are the dominant types of soils.
One of the major environmental problems in Eritrea is soil erosion.
Erosion reduces moisture-holding capacity and makes the soil less capable of supporting crop production.
To alleviate the problem, farmers in Eritrea practice a wide range soil conservation measures that include terracing, contour ploughing, shelter belts, check dams, reforestation and inter-cropping.
Degradation: Erosion after trees are cut, overgrazing, steep farming without terraces, erratic rain, loss of organic matter.
Conservation: Terraces and bunds, afforestation, check dams, crop rotation / manure, controlled grazing, keep vegetation on slopes.

questions.q: Which of the following is **incorrect** about soils in Eritrea?

options.A: Soils of the lowland are coarse in texture.
options.B: Soils in the lowlands have low permeability.
options.C: Soils in the arid areas contain a high amount of soluble salts.
options.D: Fluvial soils are found in the flood plains of the streams.

why: Statement B is incorrect because lowland soils (especially in the Western and Eastern lowlands) are often **sandy and coarse**, which gives them **high permeability** (water passes through easily), not low permeability.

questions.q: The build-up of salts in irrigated soils in hot, dry areas is called ____.

similar.a: Washing of nutrients downward out of the topsoil by water.

why: Answer D: salinisation
In hot climates irrigation water evaporates quickly.
Dissolved salts are left at the surface.
This salinisation makes soil less fertile.
